questions.stem: A book rests on a table. The weight of the book is $5$ N. State the size and direction of the upward force exerted by the table on the book, and explain how you know.
markscheme: B1: $5$ N upwards (equal to the weight, opposite in direction)
B1: the book is stationary, so the forces on it are balanced (no resultant force)
questions.modelAnswer: The table pushes up on the book with a force of $5$ N upwards. Because the book is not moving, there is no resultant force on it, so the upward contact force must exactly balance the $5$ N weight pulling down.

questions.stem: Two bar magnets are brought close together. State what happens when (a) a north pole is brought near a south pole, and (b) a north pole is brought near another north pole.
markscheme: B1: (a) the poles attract each other (unlike poles attract)
B1: (b) the poles repel each other (like poles repel)
questions.modelAnswer: (a) A north pole and a south pole are unlike poles, so the magnets attract each other. (b) Two north poles are like poles, so the magnets repel each other — they push apart.

questions.stem: A sprinter runs $100$ m in $20$ s. Calculate her average speed.
questions.modelAnswer: Average speed is distance divided by time: $v = \dfrac{100}{20} = 5$. Answer: $5$ m/s.

questions.stem: A resistor of $6$ Ω is connected across a $12$ V battery. Calculate the current flowing through the resistor.
questions.modelAnswer: Rearrange Ohm's law $V = IR$ to $I = \dfrac{V}{R}$. Substitute: $I = \dfrac{12}{6} = 2$. Answer: $2$ A.

questions.stem: A metal block has a mass of $240$ g and a volume of $30$ cm$^3$. Calculate the density of the metal.
questions.modelAnswer: Density is mass divided by volume: $\rho = \dfrac{240}{30} = 8$. Answer: $8$ g/cm$^3$.

questions.stem: A water wave has a frequency of $50$ Hz and a wavelength of $0.1$ m. Calculate the speed of the wave.
questions.modelAnswer: Use the wave equation $v = f\lambda$: $v = 50 \times 0.1 = 5$. Answer: $5$ m/s.

questions.stem: A see-saw is balanced on a pivot at its centre. A child of weight $300$ N sits $2$ m to the left of the pivot. A second child of weight $200$ N sits on the right-hand side. Calculate how far from the pivot the second child must sit for the see-saw to balance.
markscheme: M1: principle of moments used (clockwise moment $=$ anticlockwise moment)
questions.modelAnswer: For balance, the moments about the pivot must be equal. The left moment is $300 \times 2 = 600$ N m. Set the right moment equal: $200 \times d = 600$, so $d = \dfrac{600}{200} = 3$. The second child must sit $3$ m from the pivot.

questions.stem: A radioactive sample contains $800$ undecayed nuclei. The isotope has a half-life of $3$ days. Calculate how many undecayed nuclei remain after $9$ days.
questions.modelAnswer: Nine days is $9 \div 3 = 3$ half-lives. After the first half-life $400$ nuclei remain, after the second $200$, and after the third $100$. Answer: $100$ undecayed nuclei.
